title: NCBI GEO Submission of human whole blood transcriptomes in response to a high-fat meal
characteristic_names: study subject id #|Sex|test day|time of blood draw|coded/blinded study arm|unblinded study arm
overall_design: We used a sequencing method to observe the expression of all the genes in blood cells in five participants who were each fed a high fat meal on three separate days, resulting in 45 whole blood transcriptomes. For each sample, 3 mL of venous whole blood was drawn into a Tempus Blood RNA tube, shaken vigorously, and then frozen at -80°C until use. Total RNA was purified with the Tempus Spin RNA Isolation Kit with minor modifications to the manufacturer’s protocol. To remove residual genomic DNA, RNA samples were treated on-column with RNase-Free DNase per manufacturer’s instructions. RNA quantity, quality, and integrity were assessed with NanoDrop 1000 and 2100 Bioanalyzer. All isolated RNA had A260/A280 ratios greater than 2 and RNA integrity numbers higher than 7.3. RNA-Seq libraries were constructed at the DNA Technologies and Expression Core at the University of California, Davis, using the Ovation Human Blood RNA-Seq Library System (NuGEN Technologies). Sequencing was performed in a 2x100bp format with 45 samples multiplexed on 3 lanes on an Illumina HiSeq 4000. Analysis of the data is reported in the manuscript, “Temporal changes in postprandial blood transcriptomes reveal subject-specific pattern of expression of innate immunity genes after a high-fat meal.”

title: Dysregulated NK-cell gene expression defines the enduring symptoms of long COVID-19
overall_design: The study design comprised a cross-sectional comparison of three participant groups: healthy controls with no history of SARS-CoV-2 infection or COVID-19 vaccination (HC; n=66), individuals who had recovered from mild–severe SARS-CoV-2 infection (convalescent, CONV; n=35), and participants with long-term COVID-19 syndrome (LTCS; n=114). Blood/PBMC samples were collected and profiled using complementary immune assays. Humoral immunity was assessed using a 3-plex SARS-CoV-2 antibody panel (HC n=66; CONV n=24; LTCS n=94), systemic inflammation was quantified using a 13-plex inflammation panel (HC n=66; CONV n=24; LTCS n=86), and cellular immune composition was characterized by 14-color immunophenotyping (HC n=9; CONV n=6; LTCS n=23). In a subset of participants, PBMCs were additionally analyzed by single-cell RNA sequencing using the Parse Biosciences Evercode combinatorial barcoding platform (HC n=8; CONV n=6; LTCS n=32) to resolve cell-type–specific transcriptional programs associated with convalescence and long-term COVID-19.

title: Cellular and immunometabolic mechanisms of inflammation in depression: Preliminary findings from single cell RNA sequencing
overall_design: Samples were analyzed from six patients with major depression. All patients were female and non-Hispanic African Americans to limit demographic differences. Patients were stratified into high plasma C-reactive protein [CRP] (>3 mg/L; n = 3) and low plasma CRP (≤3 mg/L; n = 3) groups. Samples from patients with high CRP were obtained both before and 2 weeks after a single infusion of infliximab (5 mg/kg) for a total of 9 samples.  Fasting whole blood samples were collected between 8 and 10 a.m. after 30 min of rest (to avoid circadian influences and effects of stress) in chilled EDTA tubes. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were isolated from EDTA whole blood on Histopaque-1077. After washing, cells were counted, and 3-5 million cells were resuspended in sterile freezing media (90% FBS and 10% DMSO). Cells were slowly frozen in an isopropanol-containing cryopreservation vessel at -80C for 24 h then stored in liquid nitrogen.  Upon thawing for sequencing, cells were washed and resuspended in PBS+ 0.04%BSA. The quantity and quality of the cells were accessed by Acridine Orange and Propidium iodide dye on a Cellometer Auto 2000 (Nexcelom). Dead cell removal was performed per manufacturer’s recommendation using Miltenyi Biotec Dead Cell Removal (Miltenyi Biotec, Bergisch Gladbach, Germany). 7000 cells with the viability higher than 70% were loaded on a 10x Chromium Controller using 10X Genomics 3’ GEX v3.1 Platform (10x Genomics). After cell partitioning and GEM generation, reverse transcription was performed, and cDNA was pooled and cleaned up by beads. cDNA was further amplified for 13 cycles and cleaned up by SPRI beads (Beckman). Final library was constructed using 10X Genomics 3’ GEX v3.1 (10x Genomics) based on manufacturer’s manual. The quality of FL was assessed by High Sensitivity D5000 Tapestation (Agilent Technologies Inc., California, USA) and quantified by Qubit 2.0 DNA HS assay (ThermoFisher, Massachusetts, USA). The average final library size is 400bp with an insert size of about 250bp. Equimolar pooling of libraries was performed based on QC values and sequenced on an Illumina® Hiseq X (Illumina, California, USA) with a read length configuration of 150 PE targeting for 100M total reads per sample (50M in each direction).
